### Plane Get an audit log

Get an audit log in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the audit log entry to retrieve. This is the entry's `id`, not its `event_id`. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `actor_display_name`, `actor_email`, `actor_id`, `actor_type`, `category`, `created_at`, `event_id`, `event_name`, `id`, `ip_address`, `metadata`, `new_value`, `old_value`, `outcome`, `project_id`, `reason`, `sequence_number`, `source`, `target_display_name`, `target_id`, `target_type`, `user_agent`, `workspace_id`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Audit- Logs |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for this audit log record. This is the id you pass to \[Get an audit log\]\(/api-reference/v2/audit-logs/get-audit-log\). |
|   ↳ `event_id` | string | Identifier of the event the record describes, distinct from `id`. Use it as the idempotency key when you ingest entries into another system so a re-read never double-counts. |
|   ↳ `sequence_number` | number | An ordering number assigned to the entry as it was written. Useful as a stable tiebreaker when two entries share the same `created_at`. |
|   ↳ `event_name` | string | The specific event, for example `member.role_updated`. Filterable — this is the field to pin when you know exactly which action you are hunting for. |
|   ↳ `category` | string | The family the event belongs to. One of `auth`, `member`, `role`, `settings`, `integration`, `webhook`, `security`, or `instance`. Filter on `category` when you want a whole class of activity rather than one event name. |
|   ↳ `outcome` | string | Whether the attempt succeeded. One of `success` or `failure`. Failed attempts are recorded, which is what makes this useful for detecting probing. |
|   ↳ `source` | string | The surface the request came through. One of `platform`, `api`, `graphql`, `auth`, `admin`, or `system`. `api` marks calls made with a token like yours; `admin` marks actions taken through instance God Mode; `system` marks actions Plane took on its own. |
|   ↳ `actor_type` | string | What kind of principal acted. One of `user`, `api_token`, `system`, or `anonymous`. |
|   ↳ `actor_id` | string | Actor id |
|   ↳ `actor_display_name` | string | Actor display name |
|   ↳ `actor_email` | string | Actor email |
|   ↳ `target_type` | string | The kind of thing that was acted on, for example `workspace_member`. |
|   ↳ `target_id` | string | Identifier of the thing that was acted on. |
|   ↳ `target_display_name` | string | A human-readable label for the target, captured at the time of the event. |
|   ↳ `old_value` | object | Old value |
|     ↳ `role` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `new_value` | object | New value |
|     ↳ `role` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `reason` | string | A short explanation recorded alongside the event. Most informative on `outcome: failure` entries. |
|   ↳ `metadata` | json | Metadata |
|     ↳ `workspace_slug` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `ip_address` | string | Ip address |
|   ↳ `user_agent` | string | The client's user agent string. |
|   ↳ `workspace_id` | string | The workspace the event belongs to. |
|   ↳ `project_id` | json | Project id |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the event was recorded. This is the field the date-range filters work on. |

### Plane Get a cycle

Get a cycle in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the cycle belongs to. A cycle id from a different project returns `404`, not the record. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The cycle to retrieve. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `end_date`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `logo_props`, `name`, `owned_by_id`, `sort_order`, `start_date`, `timezone`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `owned_by` \(the cycle owner\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Cycles |
|   ↳ `id` | json | Id |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | json | Description |
|   ↳ `start_date` | string | Start date |
|   ↳ `end_date` | string | End date |
|   ↳ `timezone` | json | Timezone |
|   ↳ `owned_by_id` | string | The user who owns the cycle. Read-only — assigned by Plane and not settable through the API. Use it to filter cycles on list. |
|   ↳ `sort_order` | json | Sort order |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | json | Created at |
|   ↳ `created_by_id` | string | The user who created the cycle. |
|   ↳ `owned_by` | json | Owned by |
|   ↳ `total_issues` | json | Total issues |
|   ↳ `cancelled_issues` | json | Cancelled issues |
|   ↳ `completed_issues` | json | Completed issues |
|   ↳ `started_issues` | json | Started issues |
|   ↳ `unstarted_issues` | json | Unstarted issues |
|   ↳ `backlog_issues` | json | Backlog issues |
|   ↳ `total_estimates` | number | Total estimates |
|   ↳ `completed_estimates` | number | Completed estimates |
|   ↳ `started_estimates` | number | Started estimates |
|   ↳ `updated_at` | string | Updated at |
|   ↳ `deleted_at` | string | Deleted at |
|   ↳ `view_props` | json | View props |
|   ↳ `progress_snapshot` | json | Progress snapshot |
|   ↳ `archived_at` | string | Archived at |
|   ↳ `version` | json | Version |
|   ↳ `created_by` | string | Created by |
|   ↳ `updated_by` | string | Updated by |
|   ↳ `project` | string | Project |
|   ↳ `workspace` | string | Workspace |
|   ↳ `status` | string | Status |
|   ↳ `deleted_by` | json | Deleted by |

### Plane Get a module

Get a module in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the module belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The module to retrieve. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `lead_id`, `logo_props`, `member_ids`, `name`, `sort_order`, `start_date`, `status`, `target_date`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `lead` \(the module lead\), `members` \(the module members\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |

### Plane Get a property context

Get a property context in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `property_id` | string | Yes | The workspace-level property the context belongs to. A project-level property id is not addressable here and returns `404 not_found`. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the context to retrieve. A context that belongs to a different property returns `404`, even if the id exists. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `applies_to_all_projects`, `applies_to_all_work_item_types`, `created_at`, `default_value`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `is_default`, `is_multi`, `is_required`, `issue_type_ids`, `name`, `options`, `project_ids`, `settings`, `sort_order`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Item- Property- Contexts |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the context. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, unique among the contexts of this property. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `is_required` | boolean | Whether the property must be filled in inside this scope. Overrides the property's own `is_required`. |
|   ↳ `is_multi` | boolean | Whether the property accepts several values inside this scope. Overrides the property's own `is_multi`. |
|   ↳ `is_default` | boolean | `true` on the context Plane seeded with the property. It is a marker only — precedence is decided by the scope flags, not by this field. |
|   ↳ `default_value` | array | Values applied when a work item in this scope has nothing set. For `OPTION` properties, options in this context flagged `is_default` take precedence over this array. |
|   ↳ `settings` | json | Settings |
|   ↳ `sort_order` | json | Sort order |
|   ↳ `applies_to_all_projects` | boolean | When `true`, the context covers every project in the workspace and `project_ids` is empty. When `false`, `project_ids` is the exact list of projects covered. |
|   ↳ `applies_to_all_work_item_types` | boolean | When `true`, the context covers every work item type and `issue_type_ids` is empty. When `false`, `issue_type_ids` is the exact list of types covered. |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the context was created. |
|   ↳ `project_ids` | array | The ids of the projects this context covers. Empty when `applies_to_all_projects` is `true` — read the flag before reading this list. |
|   ↳ `issue_type_ids` | array | The ids of the work item types this context covers. Empty when `applies_to_all_work_item_types` is `true`. |
|   ↳ `options` | array | The choices this context offers for an `OPTION` property. Each entry has `id`, `name`, `is_default`, and `sort_order`. Options belong to a context, not to the property, so two contexts on the same property can offer different lists. |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Has Pages |
|     ↳ `sort_order` | number | Access |

|   ↳ `group` | json | Group |
|   ↳ `sequence` | json | Sequence |

|   ↳ `updated_by` | string | Updated by |
|   ↳ `project` | string | Project |
|   ↳ `workspace` | string | Workspace |
|   ↳ `slug` | string | Slug |

|   ↳ `validation_rules` | json | Validation rules |

| `pk` | string | Yes | The work item's UUID. This lookup is UUID-only — a `PROJ-142` identifier here returns `404`. |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `assignees` \(the assigned users\), `cycle` \(the cycle it belongs to\), `labels` \(the applied labels\), `modules` \(the modules it belongs to\), `parent` \(its parent work item\), `state` \(the work item's state object\), `type` \(its work item type\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `assignee_ids`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `custom_fields`, `cycle_id`, `id`, `identifier`, `is_draft`, `label_ids`, `module_ids`, `name`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `project_id`, `sequence_id`, `start_date`, `state_id`, `target_date`, `type_id`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `external_id` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. External system identifier for filtering or lookup |
| `external_source` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. External system source name for filtering or lookup |
| `order_by` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Field to order results by. Prefix with '-' for descending order |

### Plane Get a work item by identifier

Get a work item by identifier in Plane. Requires API v2.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

The project part must start with a letter, and it is upper-cased before lookup, so `proj-142` resolves the same work item as `PROJ-142`. A project identifier is unique within a workspace, which is what makes this key unambiguous. |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `assignees` \(the assigned users\), `cycle` \(the cycle it belongs to\), `labels` \(the applied labels\), `modules` \(the modules it belongs to\), `parent` \(its parent work item\), `state` \(the work item's state object\), `type` \(its work item type\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `assignee_ids`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `custom_fields`, `cycle_id`, `id`, `identifier`, `is_draft`, `label_ids`, `module_ids`, `name`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `project_id`, `sequence_id`, `start_date`, `state_id`, `target_date`, `type_id`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |

| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the property to retrieve. |

Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Item- Properties |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the property. This is the id you pass when attaching the property to a type or managing its options. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | The machine-readable slug for the property, derived by Plane. Read-only — it is not a create or update body field. Use it when you need a stable key in your own storage. |
|   ↳ `display_name` | string | The human-readable label shown wherever the property is rendered. This is the field you **write** on create and update. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | string | Free-form explanation of what the field is for. Surfaced as helper text next to the field. |
|   ↳ `property_type` | string | What kind of data the property holds. One of `TEXT`, `DATETIME`, `DECIMAL`, `BOOLEAN`, `OPTION`, `RELATION`, `URL`, `EMAIL`, `FILE`, or `FORMULA`. See the \[property type reference\]\(#property-type-reference\) below. |
|   ↳ `relation_type` | string | Relation type |
|   ↳ `is_multi` | boolean | Whether the property accepts more than one value. A multi-select severity list, a set of assignable reviewers, several linked work items. |
|   ↳ `is_required` | boolean | Whether a value must be present. Turning this on for an existing property affects work items edited from then on — it does not retroactively fill in the blanks. |
|   ↳ `is_active` | boolean | Whether the property is currently offered. Deactivating is the reversible alternative to deleting: the definition and its recorded values stay, the field stops being offered on new edits. |
|   ↳ `default_value` | array | The value applied when none is supplied. Always an array, even for a single-valued property — a decimal that defaults to `3` is `\["3"\]`, not `3`. |
|   ↳ `options` | array | For `OPTION` properties, the resolved list of choices. Each entry is a property option object with its own `id`, `name`, `is_default`, and `sort_order`. ### Plane Get a work item type schema

Get a work item type schema in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the type belongs to. The schema is project-specific: states, labels, members, and estimate points all come from this project. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the work item type whose schema you want. |
| `include` | string | No | Comma-separated extra option lists to inline. Two values are recognized: - `members` — inlines the project's active members as the options for `assignee_ids`, and for any custom property that is a user relation - `labels` — inlines the project's labels as the options for `label_ids` Omit it and those fields still appear, they just describe themselves without an option list. These lists can be large in a big workspace, so ask for them only when you are actually rendering a picker — for example `?include=members,labels`. |
| `fields` | string | No | The standard work item fields, keyed by the body parameter name you would send — `name`, `description_html`, `priority`, `state_id`, `assignee_ids`, `label_ids`, `start_date`, `target_date`, `parent_id`. Each entry carries a `type`, a `required` flag, and where it applies an `is_multi` flag, a `default`, a `max_length`, a `format`, or an `options` array. `state_id` and `priority` always arrive with their options inlined, because those are the two fields a client cannot guess. `estimate_point_id` appears only when the project has an estimate system configured. |

|   ↳ `customers` | boolean | Customers |

|   ↳ `pi` | boolean | Pi |

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |

| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Workspace- Work- Item- Type- Properties |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the property. This is the id you send in `properties` to attach it, and the `pk` you use to detach it. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Read-only companion to `display_name`. You never set it directly. |
|   ↳ `display_name` | string | The label shown wherever the property is rendered. |
|   ↳ `description` | string | Description |
|   ↳ `property_type` | string | What kind of value the property holds. One of `TEXT`, `DATETIME`, `DECIMAL`, `BOOLEAN`, `OPTION`, `RELATION`, `URL`, `EMAIL`, `FILE`, or `FORMULA`. |
|   ↳ `relation_type` | string | Relation type |
|   ↳ `is_required` | boolean | Whether a value must be supplied for this property. |
|   ↳ `is_multi` | boolean | Whether the property accepts more than one value. |
|   ↳ `is_active` | boolean | Whether the property is in use. A property can be retired by setting this to `false` on the catalog resource, without deleting it. |
|   ↳ `default_value` | array | The value applied when none is supplied. Always an array, even when `is_multi` is `false`. |
|   ↳ `options` | array | The choices for an `OPTION` property. Manage them through \[Property options\]\(/api-reference/v2/workspace-work-item-property-options/overview\). |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `description` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Has Pages |
|     ↳ `sort_order` | number | Access |
|     ↳ `external_id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `external_source` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `settings` | json | Settings |
|   ↳ `validation_rules` | json | Validation rules |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the property was created. |

Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `description`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_default`, `is_epic`, `level`, `logo_props`, `name`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Workspace- Work- Item- Types |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the type. This is the id you send as `type_id` on a work item, and the id you pass when importing types into a project. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, for example `Bug`. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | string | What this type is for. Shown next to the type wherever it is picked in Plane, so it is worth writing for the people choosing, not for your integration. |
|   ↳ `is_active` | boolean | Whether the type can currently be selected. Deactivating a type retires it from pickers without deleting it or touching the work items already using it. |

|   ↳ `is_epic` | boolean | Whether the type is an epic type. Read-only, and there is no body parameter for it: every type you create through this API is a standard work item type. |
|   ↳ `level` | json | Level |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the type was created. |

### Plane List audit logs

List audit logs in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `created_after` | string | No | Return entries recorded from this timestamp onward, for example `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Pair it with `created_before` to bound a review period. |
| `created_before` | string | No | Return entries recorded up to this timestamp. Send timestamps in UTC — `created_at` is returned in UTC, and mixing offsets is the usual reason a window looks empty. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `actor_display_name`, `actor_email`, `actor_id`, `actor_type`, `category`, `created_at`, `event_id`, `event_name`, `id`, `ip_address`, `metadata`, `new_value`, `old_value`, `outcome`, `project_id`, `reason`, `sequence_number`, `source`, `target_display_name`, `target_id`, `target_type`, `user_agent`, `workspace_id`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `actor_id` | string | No | Return only what one user did. This is the same id as `member_id` on the \[member rosters\]\(/api-reference/v2/members/overview\), so an access certification is a roster read followed by one call per person. Entries with no actor — `system` and `anonymous` events — are excluded by any `actor_id` filter, so run a second unfiltered query if you are asked to account for everything in a window. |
| `event_name` | string | No | Return only one specific event, for example `member.role_updated`. Use it when you already know the action you are hunting for; use `category` when you want a whole class of them. |
| `category` | string | No | Return only one family of events: `auth`, `member`, `role`, `settings`, `integration`, `webhook`, `security`, or `instance`. `role` and `member` answer "who gained access and when". `settings` answers "what changed about this workspace". `auth` plus `outcome=failure` answers "who tried to get in". |
| `outcome` | string | No | Return only entries with this outcome: `success` or `failure`. Failed attempts are recorded, which is what makes this filter the fastest way to spot probing. |
| `target_type` | string | No | Return only entries acting on this kind of object, for example `workspace_member`. Combine it with `target_id` to build the history of a single record. |
| `target_id` | string | No | Return only entries acting on this specific object. `?target_type=…&target_id=…` is the "everything that ever happened to this thing" query. |
| `ip_address` | string | No | Return only entries recorded from this client IP. Start from a suspicious entry, then pivot on its `ip_address` to see everything else that address did. |
| `search` | string | No | A free-text search term across the entry. Reach for it when you have a name or a fragment rather than an id. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `-created_at` , `created_at` — newest first, or oldest first - `id` , `-id` Use `-created_at` for an investigation, `created_at` for a replayable export. Two entries written in the same instant are separated by `sequence_number` in the payload. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Use 200 for exports. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000 — which an audit trail exceeds quickly, so use cursor pagination for anything deeper than a few pages. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` for the COUNT-free keyset envelope, which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. This is the mode to use for a full export: it has no offset ceiling and it does not skip or repeat rows as new entries land mid-walk. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted. Worth doing on every page of an offset walk — cursor pagination never runs a `COUNT` and ignores this parameter. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 V2 List Audit Logsresult |
|   ↳ `data` | array | Data |

### Plane List comments

List comments in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the work item belongs to. |
| `work_item_id` | string | Yes | The work item whose comments you want. Comments never span work items, so this narrows the result set by itself. |
| `access` | string | No | Return only comments with this visibility. - `INTERNAL` — visible to the project team - `EXTERNAL` — marked as visible outside the team |
| `external_id` | string | No | Return comments carrying this identifier from your system. `external_id` is not a unique key, so this can match more than one comment — pair it with `external_source` and handle a multi-row result. |
| `external_source` | string | No | Return comments that came from this system, for example `github` or `zendesk`. |
| `search` | string | No | Match comments against their plain-text body \(`comment_stripped`\), so HTML markup in `comment_html` never affects whether a term hits. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. Send it explicitly whenever order matters — a thread you render should not depend on the server's unstated default. - `created_at` — oldest first - `-created_at` — newest first - `id` - `-id` |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000 — for deeper traversal switch to cursor pagination. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into the COUNT-free keyset envelope instead of the default offset envelope. The response then carries `next_cursor` and `has_more`; send the value of `next_cursor` back as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page. See \[Pagination\]\(/api-reference/v2/pagination\) for the full envelope. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` and omit `total_count` from the offset envelope. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `access`, `actor_id`, `comment_html`, `comment_stripped`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `edited_at`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `work_item_id`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `actor` \(the comment author\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

### Plane List cycles

List cycles in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project whose cycles you want. |
| `owned_by_id` | string | No | Return only cycles owned by this user. This is how you build a "my cycles" view — pass the authenticated user's id. Ownership is assigned by Plane, so this is a read-side filter only. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Return only cycles whose `external_id` matches exactly. Pair it with `external_source` when the same identifier could come from more than one system. |
| `external_source` | string | No | Return only cycles imported from this source, for example `jira`. |
| `search` | string | No | Free-text search term matched against the cycle. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `sort_order` / `-sort_order` — the project's manual cycle ordering - `created_at` / `-created_at` — newest or oldest first - `id` / `-id` |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000 — past that, switch to cursor pagination. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into the COUNT-free keyset envelope instead of the default offset envelope. The response then carries `next_cursor` and `has_more` rather than `next`, `previous`, and `total_count`; pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to walk to the following page. Use it for deep traversal, where offset paging gets expensive. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count` — the field is then omitted from the envelope. Worth doing when you only need the rows. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `end_date`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `logo_props`, `name`, `owned_by_id`, `sort_order`, `start_date`, `timezone`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `owned_by` \(the cycle owner\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |
| `cycle_view` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter cycles by status |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |

### Plane List invitations

| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `accepted` | boolean | No | Filter by `accepted`. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Set to false to skip the total_count COUNT\(\*\) \(omits total_count\). |
| `email` | string | No | Filter by `email`. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to order the list by. Prefix with '-' for descending \(e.g. '-created_at'\). Annotation-backed orders sort semantically and ride the default offset page. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to 'cursor' to opt into the COUNT-free keyset cursor envelope \(use for deep traversal\); omit for the default offset envelope with total_count. One of `cursor`. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size \(max 200\). |
| `search` | string | No | A search term. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from each row, not returned as `null`. `id` always comes back. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that names the valid set, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). Requestable here: `accepted`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `email`, `id`, `message`, `responded_at`, `role`. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

### Plane List labels

List labels in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project whose labels you want. |
| `parent_id` | string | No | Return only the labels nested under this label. Pair it with `parent_id__isnull=true` to get the opposite view — every top-level label in the project. Use `parent_id__isnull=false` for every label that has a parent. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Return labels whose `external_id` matches. Combine with `external_source` to resolve a record from another system to its Plane label without keeping a local id map. |
| `external_source` | string | No | Return labels that came from this system, for example `github` or `jira`. |
| `search` | string | No | A search term matched against the label `name`. Use it to power type-ahead in a picker rather than downloading every page and filtering client-side. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. Defaults to `sort_order`. - `sort_order` , `-sort_order` — the project's own label ordering - `created_at` , `-created_at` — newest or oldest first - `id` , `-id` A value outside this list is not rejected — it silently falls back to the default `sort_order`. Check your spelling: a typo in `order_by` fails silently and shows up as a differently sorted page, not as an error. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read the `next` value from the response and send it back as `offset` to walk forward. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to switch from the default offset envelope to the keyset cursor envelope, which skips the `COUNT\(*\)` and returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Send the returned `next_cursor` back as `cursor` to fetch the following page. Only `created_at` and `id` are cursor-eligible, because a keyset needs a strictly ordered column and `sort_order` is neither unique nor monotonic. Pair `paginate=cursor` with `order_by=created_at` or `order_by=id` — the default `sort_order` ordering is rejected with `400 ordering_not_cursor_eligible`. Most projects have few enough labels that the default offset envelope is all you need. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to omit `total_count` and skip the count query. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `color`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `name`, `parent_id`, `sort_order`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |
| `expand` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Comma-separated list of related fields to expand in response |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 V2 List Labelsresult |
|   ↳ `data` | array | Data |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the label. This is the value you send in a work item's `label_ids`. |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. |
|     ↳ `description` | string | Free-form note about what the label is for. Useful when a team needs a convention written down next to the tag. |
|     ↳ `color` | string | Hex color used wherever the label is rendered, for example `#e5484d`. |
|     ↳ `sort_order` | json | Sort Order |
|     ↳ `parent_id` | string | The label this one nests under, letting you build groups such as an `Area` label with `Billing` and `Search` beneath it. `null` for a top-level label. |
|     ↳ `external_id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `external_source` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `created_at` | string | When the label was created. |
|     ↳ `created_by_id` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `next` | number | Next |

### Plane List modules

List modules in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project whose modules you want. |
| `status` | string | No | Return only modules in this lifecycle position. One of `backlog`, `planned`, `in-progress`, `paused`, `completed`, or `cancelled`. Use `status__in` with a comma-separated list to match several at once, for example `?status__in=planned,in-progress`. |
| `lead_id` | string | No | Return only modules led by this user. Match is exact on the module's `lead_id`. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Return only modules carrying this external identifier. Pair it with `external_source` to resolve a record you imported from another system. |
| `external_source` | string | No | Return only modules that came from this system, for example `github` or `jira`. |
| `search` | string | No | Free-text match on the module name. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `sort_order` , `-sort_order` - `created_at` , `-created_at` - `id` , `-id` Defaults to `sort_order`. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000 — go deeper with cursor pagination. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into the COUNT-free keyset envelope, then follow `next_cursor` with `?cursor=`. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Set to `false` to skip the count query and omit `total_count` from the offset envelope. Defaults to `true`. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `lead_id`, `logo_props`, `member_ids`, `name`, `sort_order`, `start_date`, `status`, `target_date`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `status__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Return only modules in this lifecycle position. One of `backlog`, `planned`, `in-progress`, `paused`, `completed`, or `cancelled`. Use `status__in` with a comma-separated list to match several at once, for example `?status__in=planned,in-progress`. |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `lead` \(the module lead\), `members` \(the module members\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

### Plane List project members

List project members in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project whose roster you want. A project id from another workspace returns `404`. |
| `member_id` | string | No | Return the membership for one user. Use `member_id__in` to check several at once, comma-separated. Pairing `?member_id=` with `?per_page=1` is the cheapest membership check there is: an empty `data` array means that user is not on this project. |
| `role` | string | No | Return only members holding this role slug, for example `?role=contributor`. Use `role__in` for several roles at once, comma-separated. The value is a plain string, not a fixed enum — a custom role is matched by its own slug. |
| `search` | string | No | A search term matched against the member's user record, so you can find someone by name or email without expanding first. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `id`, `member_id`, `role`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `member_id__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Return the membership for one user. Use `member_id__in` to check several at once, comma-separated. Pairing `?member_id=` with `?per_page=1` is the cheapest membership check there is: an empty `data` array means that user is not on this project. |
| `role__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Return only members holding this role slug, for example `?role=contributor`. Use `role__in` for several roles at once, comma-separated. The value is a plain string, not a fixed enum — a custom role is matched by its own slug. |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `member` \(the member's user object\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `created_at` , `-created_at` — when the person was added to the project - `id` , `-id` |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Most project rosters fit in a single page. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read `next` from the response rather than computing offsets yourself. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` for the COUNT-free keyset envelope, which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 V2 List Project Membersresult |
|   ↳ `data` | array | Data |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the membership row — not for the user. The same person has one membership in the workspace and another in each project they belong to, so they have several `id` values but one `member_id`. |

|       ↳ `display_name` | string | Asset Id |
|       ↳ `avatar_url` | string | Asset Id |
|       ↳ `email` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `next` | number | Next |
|   ↳ `previous` | number | Previous |
|   ↳ `total_count` | number | Total count |
|   ↳ `pagination` | object | Pagination |
|     ↳ `style` | string | Style |
|   ↳ `next_cursor` | string | Next cursor |
|   ↳ `has_more` | boolean | Has more |
| `results` | array | Returned Plane records. |

### Plane List property contexts

List property contexts in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `property_id` | string | Yes | The workspace-level property whose contexts you want. A project-level property id is not addressable here and returns `404 not_found`. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `applies_to_all_projects`, `applies_to_all_work_item_types`, `created_at`, `default_value`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `is_default`, `is_multi`, `is_required`, `issue_type_ids`, `name`, `options`, `project_ids`, `settings`, `sort_order`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `sort_order` , `-sort_order` — the property's own context order. This is the default. - `created_at` , `-created_at` — when each context was added - `id` , `-id` |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. A property usually has a handful of contexts, so one page is normally the whole set. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read the `next` value from the response rather than computing offsets yourself. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into the COUNT-free keyset envelope, which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Pair it with `order_by=created_at` or `order_by=id` — the default `sort_order` ordering is not unique, so it is not cursor-eligible and the request is rejected with `ordering_not_cursor_eligible`. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

|     ↳ `is_multi` | boolean | Whether the property accepts several values inside this scope. Overrides the property's own `is_multi`. |
|     ↳ `is_default` | boolean | `true` on the context Plane seeded with the property. It is a marker only — precedence is decided by the scope flags, not by this field. |

### Plane List states

List states in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project whose states you want to list. |
| `group` | string | No | Return only states in this workflow group. One of `backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed`, `cancelled`, or `triage`. Use the `group__in` variant to match several groups at once, passing them comma-separated — `?group__in=started,completed`. Filtering by group is the portable way to ask "what counts as in progress here", because every project names its states differently but the groups are fixed. |
| `is_default` | boolean | No | Return only the project's default state \(`true`\) or only the non-default states \(`false`\). Pairing `?is_default=true` with `?per_page=1` is the cheapest way to find where new work items will land. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Return states whose `external_id` matches exactly. Use it to find the state you previously created for a record in another system. |
| `external_source` | string | No | Return states that came from a particular system, for example `github` or `jira`. Combine it with `external_id` — an `external_id` is only unique within its source. |
| `search` | string | No | A search term matched against the state name. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `color`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `group`, `id`, `is_default`, `is_triage`, `name`, `sequence`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `group__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Return only states in this workflow group. One of `backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed`, `cancelled`, or `triage`. Use the `group__in` variant to match several groups at once, passing them comma-separated — `?group__in=started,completed`. Filtering by group is the portable way to ask "what counts as in progress here", because every project names its states differently but the groups are fixed. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `sequence` , `-sequence` — the project's own workflow order - `created_at` , `-created_at` — when each state was added - `id` , `-id` Order by `sequence` when you are rendering the workflow to a user; it is the order the project itself uses. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Most projects have fewer than 20 states, so one page is usually the whole workflow. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read the `next` value from the response rather than computing offsets yourself. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into the COUNT-free keyset envelope, which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Omit it for the default offset envelope. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |
| `expand` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Comma-separated list of related fields to expand in response |

Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `default_value`, `description`, `display_name`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_multi`, `is_required`, `logo_props`, `name`, `options`, `property_type`, `relation_type`, `settings`, `validation_rules`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `sort_order` , `-sort_order` — the order the properties are shown in, and the default - `created_at` , `-created_at` — when each property was created - `id` , `-id` Order by `sort_order` when you are rendering the type's form to a user; it is the order Plane itself uses. Note that `sort_order` is not part of the returned property object — sort by `created_at` or `id` if you need the sort key to be visible in the payload. |

### Plane List work item types

List work item types in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project whose work item types you want to list. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `description`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_default`, `is_epic`, `level`, `logo_props`, `name`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `level` , `-level` — the type hierarchy level - `name` , `-name` — alphabetical - `created_at` , `-created_at` — when each type was added - `id` , `-id` Order by `level` when you are rendering types to a user; it is the order the project itself uses. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Most projects define a handful of types, so one page is usually the whole set. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read the `next` value from the response rather than computing offsets yourself. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into the COUNT-free keyset envelope, which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Omit it for the default offset envelope. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `assignee_ids`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `cycle_id`, `id`, `identifier`, `is_draft`, `label_ids`, `module_ids`, `name`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `project_id`, `sequence_id`, `start_date`, `state_id`, `target_date`, `type_id`. Naming `custom_fields` here is a `400` — it is only available on single-object responses. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `state_id` | string | No | Match work items in a specific state. Use `state_id__in` with a comma-separated list to match any of several states. |
| `state_id__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Match work items in a specific state. Use `state_id__in` with a comma-separated list to match any of several states. |
| `state_group` | string | No | Match by the state's workflow group instead of a specific state — stable across projects that name their states differently. One of `backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `triage`. Use `state_group__in` for several groups, for example `?state_group__in=started,completed`. |
| `state_group__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Match by the state's workflow group instead of a specific state — stable across projects that name their states differently. One of `backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `triage`. Use `state_group__in` for several groups, for example `?state_group__in=started,completed`. |
| `priority` | string | No | One of `urgent`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `none`. Use `priority__in` for several, for example `?priority__in=urgent,high`. |

| `type_id__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Match work items of a given work item type. `type_id__in` accepts a comma-separated list. |
| `parent_id` | string | No | Match the children of a work item. `parent_id__in` accepts several parents; `parent_id__isnull=true` returns only top-level work items. |
| `parent_id__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Match the children of a work item. `parent_id__in` accepts several parents; `parent_id__isnull=true` returns only top-level work items. |
| `cycle_id` | string | No | Match work items in a cycle. `cycle_id__in` accepts several cycles; `cycle_id__isnull=true` returns the backlog of work items in no cycle at all. |
| `cycle_id__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Match work items in a cycle. `cycle_id__in` accepts several cycles; `cycle_id__isnull=true` returns the backlog of work items in no cycle at all. |
| `module_id` | string | No | Match work items in a module. `module_id__in` accepts several modules; `module_id__isnull=true` returns work items in no module. |
| `module_id__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Match work items in a module. `module_id__in` accepts several modules; `module_id__isnull=true` returns work items in no module. |
| `sequence_id` | number | No | Match the single work item with this number within the project — the `142` of `PROJ-142`. |
| `is_draft` | boolean | No | Filter drafts in or out. Drafts are work items still being composed in the Plane app. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Correlation filters for sync and import. `external_source` is the system a record came from and `external_id` is its key there, so the pair is how you find the Plane work item that mirrors a row in your own database. These values are not returned on reads — the lookup is one-way. |
| `external_source` | string | No | Correlation filters for sync and import. `external_source` is the system a record came from and `external_id` is its key there, so the pair is how you find the Plane work item that mirrors a row in your own database. These values are not returned on reads — the lookup is one-way. |

| `created_at__lte` | string | No | Bound the creation timestamp. Pass an ISO 8601 datetime, for example `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Use both for a window. |
| `updated_at__gte` | string | No | Bound the last-modified timestamp. This is the pair to use for incremental sync — poll with `?updated_at__gte=&order_by=updated_at`. `updated_at` is filterable and orderable but is not part of the read shape, so it does not come back in the response body. |
| `updated_at__lte` | string | No | Bound the last-modified timestamp. This is the pair to use for incremental sync — poll with `?updated_at__gte=&order_by=updated_at`. `updated_at` is filterable and orderable but is not part of the read shape, so it does not come back in the response body. |
| `start_date__gte` | string | No | Bound the planned start date, for example `2026-01-01`. |
| `start_date__lte` | string | No | Bound the planned start date, for example `2026-01-01`. |
| `target_date__gte` | string | No | Bound the planned due date. `?target_date__lte=2026-01-31&state_group__in=backlog,unstarted,started` is the "what is about to slip" query. |
| `target_date__lte` | string | No | Bound the planned due date. `?target_date__lte=2026-01-31&state_group__in=backlog,unstarted,started` is the "what is about to slip" query. |
| `search` | string | No | Free-text search over the work item name. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. Defaults to `-created_at`. - `created_at`, `-created_at` - `updated_at`, `-updated_at` - `sequence_id`, `-sequence_id` - `id`, `-id` - `sort_order`, `-sort_order` — the manual board ordering - `priority`, `-priority` — semantic: `urgent` → `high` → `medium` → `low` → `none`, not alphabetical - `state_group`, `-state_group` — semantic: workflow order, not alphabetical `priority` and `state_group` sort by meaning, which is what you want for a board but is not cursor-eligible. Pair either with `?paginate=cursor` and you get `400 ordering_not_cursor_eligible`; use the default offset pages instead. |

| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into keyset pagination. The envelope changes to `next_cursor` / `has_more` and drops `total_count`. Use it for deep or long-running traversals where offset pages would drift as rows are inserted. Follow the returned `next_cursor` as described in \[Pagination\]\(/api-reference/v2/pagination\). |

| `filters` | json | No | v1 compatibility only. Structured filter expression. Requires a Plane edition with work item query filtering; Community Edition rejects this parameter. |
