### Plane List workspace members

List workspace members in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `member_id` | string | No | Return the membership for one user. Use the `member_id__in` variant to look several users up at once, comma-separated — `?member_id__in=16c61a3a-512a-48ac-b0be-b6b46fe6f430,7f2b9e04-6c1d-4a58-9e3b-0d4c8a2f6b71`. This is the cheap way to answer "is this person still in the workspace, and what is their role now?" without paging the whole roster. |
| `role` | string | No | Return only members holding this role slug, for example `?role=owner`. Use `role__in` for several roles at once, comma-separated. The value is a plain string, not a fixed enum — custom roles are matched by their own slug. |
| `search` | string | No | A search term matched against the member's user record, so you can find someone by name or email without expanding first. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `id`, `member_id`, `role`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `member_id__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Return the membership for one user. Use the `member_id__in` variant to look several users up at once, comma-separated — `?member_id__in=16c61a3a-512a-48ac-b0be-b6b46fe6f430,7f2b9e04-6c1d-4a58-9e3b-0d4c8a2f6b71`. This is the cheap way to answer "is this person still in the workspace, and what is their role now?" without paging the whole roster. |
| `role__in` | string | No | Documented filter variant. Return only members holding this role slug, for example `?role=owner`. Use `role__in` for several roles at once, comma-separated. The value is a plain string, not a fixed enum — custom roles are matched by their own slug. |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `member` \(the member's user object\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `created_at` , `-created_at` — when the person joined the workspace - `id` , `-id` There is no ordering by name or role; sort the page client-side, or expand and sort on `display_name`. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read `next` from the response rather than computing offsets yourself. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` for the COUNT-free keyset envelope, which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Worth it when you are walking a large workspace end to end. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |
| `external_id` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. External system identifier for filtering or lookup |
| `external_source` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. External system source name for filtering or lookup |
| `first_name` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter by member first name \(case-insensitive contains\) |
| `last_name` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter by member last name \(case-insensitive contains\) |
| `email` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter by member email \(case-insensitive contains\) |
| `display_name` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter by member display name \(case-insensitive contains\) |
| `role_slug` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter by role slug \(exact match\) |
| `is_active` | boolean | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter by active membership status |
| `is_bot` | boolean | No | v1 compatibility only. Filter by bot accounts |

### Plane List workspace property options

List workspace property options in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `property_id` | string | Yes | The workspace-level property whose options you want — see \[Workspace work item properties\]\(/api-reference/v2/workspace-work-item-properties/overview\). This endpoint filters options by property rather than looking the property up, so an id that isn't a workspace-level property in this workspace — including a project-scoped property id — comes back as an empty list, not a `404`. |
| `order_by` | string | No | Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. - `sort_order` , `-sort_order` — the property's own display order. This is the default. - `created_at` , `-created_at` — when each option was added - `id` , `-id` A value outside this list is ignored and the default `sort_order` ordering is used, so a typo shows up as an unexpected order rather than an error. |
| `per_page` | number | No | Page size. Defaults to 50, maximum 200. Most properties have fewer than 20 options, so one page is usually the whole list. |
| `offset` | number | No | Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Read the `next` value from the response rather than computing offsets yourself. |
| `paginate` | string | No | Set to `cursor` to opt into the COUNT-free keyset envelope, which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Omit it for the default offset envelope. Cursor pagination needs a unique, monotonic sort key, and `sort_order` is neither. Pair it with `order_by=created_at` or `order_by=id`; a bare `?paginate=cursor` falls back to the default `sort_order` ordering and is rejected with `ordering_not_cursor_eligible`. |
| `count` | boolean | No | Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT\(*\)` behind `total_count`; the field is then omitted from the response. |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 V2 List Workspace Property Optionsresult |

|     ↳ `name` | string | The choice as it is displayed. Maximum 255 characters. |
|     ↳ `description` | string | Free-form text explaining when to pick this choice. |
|     ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Whether this is the property's default choice. At most one option per property can carry it. |
|     ↳ `sort_order` | json | Sort Order |
|     ↳ `external_id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `external_source` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `next` | number | Next |
|   ↳ `previous` | number | Previous |
|   ↳ `total_count` | number | Total count |
|   ↳ `pagination` | object | Pagination |
|     ↳ `style` | string | Style |
|   ↳ `next_cursor` | string | Next cursor |
|   ↳ `has_more` | boolean | Has more |

| `parent_id__in` | json | No | Multiple values may be separated by commas. |
| `parent_id__isnull` | boolean | No | Filter by `parent_id__isnull`. |

| `priority` | string | No | - `urgent` - Urgent - `high` - High - `medium` - Medium - `low` - Low - `none` - None One of `high`, `low`, `medium`, `none`, `urgent`. |
| `priority__in` | json | No | Multiple values may be separated by commas. - `urgent` - Urgent - `high` - High - `medium` - Medium - `low` - Low - `none` - None |

| `project_id__in` | json | No | Multiple values may be separated by commas. |

| `start_date__lte` | string | No | Filter by `start_date__lte`. |

| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from each row, not returned as `null`. `id` always comes back. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that names the valid set, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). Requestable here: `archived_at`, `assignee_ids`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `cycle_id`, `id`, `identifier`, `is_draft`, `label_ids`, `module_ids`, `name`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `project_id`, `sequence_id`, `start_date`, `state_id`, `target_date`, `type_id`. |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed: `assignees`, `cycle`, `labels`, `modules`, `parent`, `state`, `type`. Expansion is separate-key — `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent: naming a relation in `?fields=` is a `400`, and expanded objects survive field filtering. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `cursor` | string | No | Cursor from next_cursor. Repeat the original filters, per_page, and order_by when following it. |

### Plane Mark a work item type as default

Mark a work item type as default in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the type belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the work item type to make the default. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `description`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_default`, `is_epic`, `level`, `logo_props`, `name`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Item- Types |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the type. This is the value you send as `type_id` when creating a work item, and the `\{type_id\}` in the type-properties paths. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, for example `Bug`. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | string | Free-form explanation of when this type should be used. Worth filling in — an integration or agent reading the \[schema endpoint\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-item-types/get-work-item-type-schema\) sees this text as `type_description` and uses it to choose between types. |
|   ↳ `is_active` | boolean | Whether the type can be assigned to new work items. Deactivating a type hides it from pickers without deleting it or touching the work items that already use it. |
|   ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Whether new work items land on this type when no `type_id` is supplied. Exactly one type per project holds the flag. It is not writable through create or update — move it with \[Mark a work item type as default\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-item-types/mark-default-work-item-type\). |
|   ↳ `is_epic` | boolean | Whether this is the project's epic type. Read-only — epics are provisioned by Plane, not authored through this endpoint. |
|   ↳ `level` | json | Level |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the type was created. |

Mark a workspace work item type as default in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the work item type to make the default. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `description`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_default`, `is_epic`, `level`, `logo_props`, `name`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Workspace- Work- Item- Types |

|   ↳ `level` | json | Level |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the type was created. |

### Plane Unarchive a work item

Unarchive a work item in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the work item belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The work item's UUID. This lookup is UUID-only — a `PROJ-142` identifier here returns `404`. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `assignee_ids`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `custom_fields`, `cycle_id`, `id`, `identifier`, `is_draft`, `label_ids`, `module_ids`, `name`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `project_id`, `sequence_id`, `start_date`, `state_id`, `target_date`, `type_id`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `assignees` \(the assigned users\), `cycle` \(the cycle it belongs to\), `labels` \(the applied labels\), `modules` \(the modules it belongs to\), `parent` \(its parent work item\), `state` \(the work item's state object\), `type` \(its work item type\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Items |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the work item. This is the `\{pk\}` on every project-scoped detail route. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Title of the work item. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `identifier` | string | The human key, for example `PROJ-142`. It is the project's identifier joined to `sequence_id`, and it is what people paste into chat and commit messages. Use it with \[Get a work item by identifier\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-items/get-work-item-by-identifier\) when you don't have the project UUID. |
|   ↳ `sequence_id` | number | The work item's number within its project. Assigned by Plane and never reused. |
|   ↳ `priority` | string | One of `urgent`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, or `none`. Never null — an unprioritized work item reads `none`. |
|   ↳ `state_id` | string | The workflow state the work item is currently in. |
|   ↳ `type_id` | string | Type id |
|   ↳ `assignee_ids` | array | User ids assigned to the work item. Empty array when unassigned. |
|   ↳ `label_ids` | array | Label ids applied to the work item. Empty array when unlabeled. |
|   ↳ `parent_id` | string | The parent work item, or `null` for a top-level item. A parent may live in another project of the same workspace. |
|   ↳ `start_date` | string | Start date |
|   ↳ `target_date` | string | Target date |
|   ↳ `is_draft` | boolean | Whether the work item is still a draft. Drafts are created in the Plane app and are excluded from most boards. |
|   ↳ `archived_at` | string | When the work item was archived, or `null` if it is active. See \[Archiving\]\(#archiving-and-deleting\). |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the work item was created. |
|   ↳ `created_by_id` | string | Created by id |
|   ↳ `custom_fields` | json | Custom fields |
|   ↳ `assignees` | array | Assignees |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `display_name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `avatar_url` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `email` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `cycle` | json | Cycle |
|   ↳ `labels` | array | Labels |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `color` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `modules` | array | Modules |
|   ↳ `parent` | object | Parent |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `sequence_id` | number | Access |
|   ↳ `state` | object | State |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `color` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `group` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `type` | object | Type |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo Props |
|     ↳ `is_epic` | boolean | Has Pages |

### Plane Update a cycle

Update a cycle in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the cycle belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The cycle to update. |
| `name` | string | No | New display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. Renaming onto a name another cycle already holds returns `409 conflict`. |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form description of what the cycle covers. |
| `start_date` | string | No | New opening date-time, in ISO 8601. Send `null` to unschedule the start. |
| `end_date` | string | No | New closing date-time, in ISO 8601. Send `null` to unschedule the end. |
| `timezone` | string | No | The IANA time zone the cycle's dates are interpreted in, for example `America/New_York` or `UTC`. Changing it re-anchors where the existing boundaries fall locally, so send it together with the dates when you are moving a cycle between regions. Any value outside the IANA list is rejected with `400 invalid_request`. |
| `sort_order` | number | No | Ordering weight for the cycle within the project. Lower values sort first when you list with `?order_by=sort_order`. |
| `logo_props` | json | No | JSON blob holding the cycle's icon configuration. Replaces the stored value outright — it is not merged key by key. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this cycle. Maximum 255 characters, nullable. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `jira`. Maximum 255 characters, nullable. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `end_date`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `logo_props`, `name`, `owned_by_id`, `sort_order`, `start_date`, `timezone`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `owned_by` \(the cycle owner\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `owned_by` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. User who owns the cycle. If not provided, defaults to the current user. |

#### Output

| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Cycles |
|   ↳ `id` | json | Id |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | json | Description |
|   ↳ `start_date` | string | Start date |
|   ↳ `end_date` | string | End date |
|   ↳ `timezone` | json | Timezone |

|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | json | Created at |
|   ↳ `created_by_id` | string | The user who created the cycle. |
|   ↳ `owned_by` | json | Owned by |
|   ↳ `total_issues` | json | Total issues |
|   ↳ `cancelled_issues` | json | Cancelled issues |
|   ↳ `completed_issues` | json | Completed issues |
|   ↳ `started_issues` | json | Started issues |
|   ↳ `unstarted_issues` | json | Unstarted issues |
|   ↳ `backlog_issues` | json | Backlog issues |
|   ↳ `total_estimates` | number | Total estimates |
|   ↳ `completed_estimates` | number | Completed estimates |
|   ↳ `started_estimates` | number | Started estimates |
|   ↳ `updated_at` | string | Updated at |
|   ↳ `deleted_at` | string | Deleted at |
|   ↳ `view_props` | json | View props |
|   ↳ `progress_snapshot` | json | Progress snapshot |

|   ↳ `updated_by` | string | Updated by |
|   ↳ `project` | string | Project |
|   ↳ `workspace` | string | Workspace |
|   ↳ `status` | string | Status |
|   ↳ `deleted_by` | json | Deleted by |

### Plane Update a label

Update a label in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the label belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The label id. |
| `name` | string | No | New display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. Renaming onto a name another label already holds returns `409 conflict`. |
| `color` | string | No | Hex color used wherever the label is rendered, for example `#e5484d`. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form note about what the label is for. |
| `parent_id` | string | No | Move the label under a different parent. The new parent must be a label in the same project. Send `null` to make the label top-level again. |
| `sort_order` | number | No | Ordering weight within the project. Lower values sort first. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this label, for sync and import correlation. Maximum 255 characters. Send `null` to clear it. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters. Send `null` to clear it. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `color`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `name`, `parent_id`, `sort_order`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

|   ↳ `parent_id` | string | Parent id |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | json | Created at |

|   ↳ `workspace` | string | Workspace |
|   ↳ `project` | string | Project |

### Plane Update a module

Update a module in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the module belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The module to update. |
| `name` | string | No | New display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. Renaming onto an existing module's name returns `409 conflict`. |
| `description` | string | No | Plain-text summary of what the module covers. |
| `status` | string | No | Move the module to a different lifecycle position. - `backlog` — Captured, not yet committed to - `planned` — Committed to but not started - `in-progress` — Actively being worked on - `paused` — Started, then put on hold - `completed` — Delivered - `cancelled` — Dropped without delivering Any value outside this list is a `400 invalid_request`. Transitions are unrestricted — a `completed` module can be sent back to `in-progress`. |
| `start_date` | string | No | Date the module is scheduled to begin, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Send `null` to clear it. |
| `target_date` | string | No | Date the module is expected to land, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Send `null` to clear it. Must not be earlier than the module's `start_date` — including the `start_date` already stored when you only send `target_date`. |
| `lead_id` | string | No | Reassign the module. Must be a member of this project — any other user id is rejected with a `400` naming `lead_id`. Send `null` to leave the module without a lead. |
| `sort_order` | number | No | Ordering weight used when modules are listed. Lower values sort first. |
| `logo_props` | json | No | Free-form JSON object holding the icon Plane renders for the module. The value you send replaces the stored object. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this module, for sync and import correlation. Maximum 255 characters. Nullable. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters. Nullable. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `lead_id`, `logo_props`, `member_ids`, `name`, `sort_order`, `start_date`, `status`, `target_date`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `lead` \(the module lead\), `members` \(the module members\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `members` | json | No | v1 compatibility only. Members. |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Modules |
|   ↳ `id` | json | Id |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | json | Description |
|   ↳ `status` | json | Status |
|   ↳ `start_date` | string | Start date |
|   ↳ `target_date` | string | Target date |
|   ↳ `lead_id` | string | Lead id |
|   ↳ `member_ids` | array | Project members assigned to the module. Read-only in v2 — module membership is not yet writable through the v2 API. |
|   ↳ `sort_order` | json | Sort order |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `archived_at` | string | Archived at |
|   ↳ `created_at` | json | Created at |
|   ↳ `created_by_id` | string | The user who created the module. |
|   ↳ `lead` | json | Lead |
|   ↳ `members` | array | Members |

|   ↳ `updated_by` | string | Updated by |
|   ↳ `project` | string | Project |
|   ↳ `workspace` | string | Workspace |
|   ↳ `deleted_by` | json | Deleted by |

### Plane Update a project

Update a project in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The project id. |
| `archive_in` | number | No | The archive in. |
| `close_in` | number | No | The close in. |
| `cover_image` | string | No | URL of the cover image. Nullable. |
| `cycle_view` | boolean | No | Whether cycle view. |
| `default_assignee_id` | string | No | Id of the related default assignee. Nullable. |
| `default_state_id` | string | No | Id of the related default state. Nullable. |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form description. |
| `emoji` | string | No | Emoji shown alongside the name. Maximum 255 characters. Nullable. |
| `estimate_id` | string | No | Id of the related estimate. Nullable. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this record, for sync and import correlation. Maximum 255 characters. Nullable. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters. Nullable. |
| `guest_view_all_features` | boolean | No | Whether guest view all features. |
| `icon_prop` | string | No | The icon prop. Nullable. |
| `identifier` | string | No | Short project key used to prefix work item numbers, for example `ENG` in `ENG-142`. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `intake_view` | boolean | No | Whether intake view. |
| `is_issue_type_enabled` | boolean | No | Whether is issue type enabled. |
| `is_time_tracking_enabled` | boolean | No | Whether is time tracking enabled. |
| `issue_views_view` | boolean | No | Whether issue views view. |
| `logo_props` | string | No | Editor-owned logo descriptor. Pass back what you read rather than composing it by hand. |
| `module_view` | boolean | No | Whether module view. |
| `name` | string | No | Display name. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `network` | string | No | Project visibility: `0` is private to members, `2` is visible to the whole workspace. |
| `page_view` | boolean | No | Whether page view. |
| `priority` | string | No | - `none` - None - `low` - Low - `medium` - Medium - `high` - High - `urgent` - Urgent One of `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent`. |

| `start_date` | string | No | Planned start date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Nullable. |
| `state_id` | string | No | Id of the related state. Nullable. |
| `target_date` | string | No | Planned due date, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Nullable. |

### Plane Update a project project automation

Update a project project automation in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the resource belongs to. Accepts the project UUID or its bare identifier, for example `ENG`. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The project automation id. |
| `description` | string | No | Automation description |
| `name` | string | No | Human-readable automation name Maximum 255 characters. |
| `project_ids` | json | No | Ids of the projects to associate. Replaces the current set. |
| `scope` | string | No | The scope defines on what entity this automation runs on \(e.g., WorkItem, Cycle, Module\) Maximum 50 characters. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted**, not returned as `null`. `id` always comes back. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). Requestable here: `bot_user_id`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `current_version_id`, `description`, `id`, `is_enabled`, `is_global`, `last_run_at`, `name`, `project_ids`, `run_count`, `scope`, `status`, `updated_at`. |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Project- Automations |
|   ↳ `actor_id` | string | The related actor. |
|   ↳ `automation_edge_id` | string | The related automation edge. |
|   ↳ `automation_id` | string | The related automation. |
|   ↳ `automation_node_id` | string | The related automation node. |
|   ↳ `automation_run_id` | string | The related automation run. |
|   ↳ `automation_scope` | string | The automation scope. |
|   ↳ `automation_version_id` | string | The related automation version. |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the record was created. |
|   ↳ `epoch` | number | The epoch. |
|   ↳ `field` | string | The field. |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier. |
|   ↳ `new_identifier` | string | The new identifier. |
|   ↳ `new_value` | string | The new value. |
|   ↳ `node_execution_id` | string | The related node execution. |
|   ↳ `old_identifier` | string | The old identifier. |
|   ↳ `old_value` | string | The old value. |
|   ↳ `verb` | string | The verb. |
|   ↳ `bot_user_id` | string | Bot user id |
|   ↳ `created_by_id` | string | Created by id |
|   ↳ `current_version_id` | string | Current version id |
|   ↳ `description` | string | Description |
|   ↳ `is_enabled` | boolean | Is enabled |
|   ↳ `is_global` | boolean | Is global |
|   ↳ `last_run_at` | string | Last run at |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Name |

|   ↳ `run_count` | number | Run count |

### Plane Update an project automation node

Update an project automation node in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |

### Plane Update a property context

Update a property context in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `property_id` | string | Yes | The workspace-level property the context belongs to. A project-level property id is not addressable here and returns `404 not_found`. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the context to update. |
| `name` | string | No | New display name, unique among this property's contexts. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `applies_to_all_projects` | boolean | No | Switch the project axis between "every project" and an explicit list. Setting it to `true` discards the context's stored `project_ids`, so the context reads back with an empty list. Setting it to `false` requires `project_ids` in the same request unless the context already has projects stored. Only one context per property may have this set to `true`, so turning it on while another context holds the slot returns `400`. |
| `project_ids` | json | No | Replace the exact set of projects this context covers. What you send becomes the whole list: ids you leave out are unlinked, and ids you add are linked. Rejected with a `400` when `applies_to_all_projects` is `true`, and when the list would be empty while the flag is `false`. Every id must belong to this workspace, and duplicates are rejected. Write-only as an input; the response echoes the stored links in `project_ids`. |
| `applies_to_all_work_item_types` | boolean | No | Switch the work item type axis between "every type" and an explicit list. Same rules as `applies_to_all_projects`: turning it on clears `issue_type_ids`, turning it off needs types to fall back on. |
| `issue_type_ids` | json | No | Replace the exact set of work item types this context covers. Same set-replacement semantics as `project_ids`, and the same validation against the wildcard flag. |
| `is_required` | boolean | No | Whether the property must be filled in inside this scope. Replaces the property's own `is_required` here. |
| `is_multi` | boolean | No | Whether the property accepts several values inside this scope. Replaces the property's own `is_multi` here. |
| `default_value` | json | No | Values applied when a work item in this scope has nothing set. For `OPTION` properties, options in this context flagged `is_default` take precedence over this array. |
| `options` | json | No | Replace this context's option list. Entries are the same shape as on create: `id` to keep an existing option, `name` to add a new one, plus optional `description` and `is_default`. An option's `sort_order` is read-only — Plane assigns it from the order of the entries you send. Sending this field rewrites the list. Any option currently on the context that you do not reference by `id` is removed, along with the values recorded through it. To keep an option and change nothing about it, include `\{ "id": "…" \}`. |
| `settings` | json | No | Type-specific configuration for this scope, as a JSON object. Replaces the property's own `settings` here. |
| `sort_order` | number | No | Ordering weight among this property's contexts. Lower values sort first. Presentational only — it does not affect which context wins for a work item. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this context. Maximum 255 characters. Must be sent together with `external_source`, and the pair must be unique within the property. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters. Must be sent together with `external_id`. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `applies_to_all_projects`, `applies_to_all_work_item_types`, `created_at`, `default_value`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `is_default`, `is_multi`, `is_required`, `issue_type_ids`, `name`, `options`, `project_ids`, `settings`, `sort_order`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Item- Property- Contexts |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the context. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, unique among the contexts of this property. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `is_required` | boolean | Whether the property must be filled in inside this scope. Overrides the property's own `is_required`. |
|   ↳ `is_multi` | boolean | Whether the property accepts several values inside this scope. Overrides the property's own `is_multi`. |
|   ↳ `is_default` | boolean | `true` on the context Plane seeded with the property. It is a marker only — precedence is decided by the scope flags, not by this field. |
|   ↳ `default_value` | array | Values applied when a work item in this scope has nothing set. For `OPTION` properties, options in this context flagged `is_default` take precedence over this array. |
|   ↳ `settings` | json | Settings |
|   ↳ `sort_order` | json | Sort order |
|   ↳ `applies_to_all_projects` | boolean | When `true`, the context covers every project in the workspace and `project_ids` is empty. When `false`, `project_ids` is the exact list of projects covered. |
|   ↳ `applies_to_all_work_item_types` | boolean | When `true`, the context covers every work item type and `issue_type_ids` is empty. When `false`, `issue_type_ids` is the exact list of types covered. |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the context was created. |
|   ↳ `project_ids` | array | The ids of the projects this context covers. Empty when `applies_to_all_projects` is `true` — read the flag before reading this list. |
|   ↳ `issue_type_ids` | array | The ids of the work item types this context covers. Empty when `applies_to_all_work_item_types` is `true`. |
|   ↳ `options` | array | The choices this context offers for an `OPTION` property. Each entry has `id`, `name`, `is_default`, and `sort_order`. Options belong to a context, not to the property, so two contexts on the same property can offer different lists. |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Has Pages |
|     ↳ `sort_order` | number | Access |

### Plane Update a state

Update a state in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the state belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The id of the state to update. |
| `name` | string | No | New display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. Renaming is safe for reporting: boards and charts key off `group`, not `name`. |
| `color` | string | No | Hex color used wherever the state is rendered, for example `#3f76ff`. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form description of what the state means in this workflow. |
| `group` | string | No | Move the state to a different workflow group. This changes how every work item in the state is counted by boards, charts, and cycle progress, so switching a state from `started` to `completed` retroactively changes what those work items report as. - `backlog` — Not yet scheduled - `unstarted` — Scheduled but not begun - `started` — Actively in progress - `completed` — Finished successfully - `cancelled` — Closed without completion - `triage` — Awaiting intake review |
| `sequence` | number | No | Ordering weight within the project. Lower values sort first. Set it to reposition the state in the workflow. |
| `is_default` | boolean | No | Make this the project's default state — where work items land when no `state_id` is supplied. A project has exactly one default, so setting this to `true` clears the flag on the state that held it. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this state, for sync and import correlation. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `color`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `group`, `id`, `is_default`, `is_triage`, `name`, `sequence`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `is_triage` | boolean | No | v1 compatibility only. Is triage. |
| `default` | boolean | No | v1 compatibility only. Default. |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 States |
|   ↳ `id` | json | Id |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, unique within the project. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | json | Description |
|   ↳ `color` | string | Hex color used wherever the state is rendered, for example `#3f76ff`. |
|   ↳ `group` | json | Group |
|   ↳ `sequence` | json | Sequence |
|   ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Whether new work items land in this state when no `state_id` is supplied. Exactly one state per project is the default. |
|   ↳ `is_triage` | json | Is triage |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | json | Created at |
|   ↳ `created_by_id` | string | The user who created the state. |
|   ↳ `updated_at` | string | Updated at |
|   ↳ `deleted_at` | string | Deleted at |
|   ↳ `default` | boolean | Default |
|   ↳ `created_by` | string | Created by |
|   ↳ `updated_by` | string | Updated by |
|   ↳ `project` | string | Project |
|   ↳ `workspace` | string | Workspace |
|   ↳ `slug` | string | Slug |
|   ↳ `deleted_by` | json | Deleted by |

### Plane Update a work item

Update a work item in Plane. Supports API v1 compatibility.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the work item belongs to. |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The work item's UUID. This lookup is UUID-only — a `PROJ-142` identifier here returns `404`. |
| `name` | string | No | New title. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `description_html` | string | No | Replacement rich-text body as HTML. Sanitized on the way in; content that can't be sanitized is rejected with a `400`. Not part of the read shape, so it won't appear in the response. |
| `priority` | string | No | One of `urgent`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `none`. |
| `state_id` | string | No | Move the work item to another state of the same project. This is the field workflow rules police — see \[Workflow rules\]\(#workflow-rules-can-reject-a-transition\). |
| `state` | string | No | The target state's **name** instead of its id, for example `Done`. Matched case-insensitively within the project. Write-only. Sending both `state` and `state_id` is a `400`. |
| `type_id` | string | No | Change the work item type. Send `null` to make the work item untyped. |
| `type` | string | No | The type's **name** instead of its id, for example `Bug`. Write-only. |
| `parent_id` | string | No | Re-parent the work item. The parent must be in the same workspace and may be in a different project. Send `null` to detach it and make it top-level. |
| `parent` | string | No | The parent's **identifier** instead of its id, for example `PROJ-118`. Write-only. |
| `assignee_ids` | json | No | **Replaces** the whole assignee set — it is not additive. Send the complete list you want, `\[\]` to unassign everyone, or omit the field to leave assignees untouched. |
| `assignees` | json | No | Member **email addresses** instead of ids. Same replace-the-set semantics. Every address must belong to an active, assignable project member. Write-only. |
| `label_ids` | json | No | **Replaces** the whole label set. Send `\[\]` to strip all labels, or omit the field to leave them untouched. |
| `labels` | json | No | Label **names** instead of ids. Same replace-the-set semantics. A name that exists at both project and workspace level is ambiguous and returns a `400` telling you to use `label_ids`. Write-only. |
| `estimate_point_id` | string | No | Change the estimate point, from the project's active estimate system. Send `null` to clear the estimate. |
| `estimate` | string | No | The estimate point's **value** instead of its id, for example `5`. Write-only. |
| `start_date` | string | No | Planned start, or `null` to clear it. Must not be after `target_date`. |
| `target_date` | string | No | Planned due date, or `null` to clear it. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this work item. Maximum 255 characters. Filterable on \[List work items\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-items/list-work-items\), but not returned on reads. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `archived_at`, `assignee_ids`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `custom_fields`, `cycle_id`, `id`, `identifier`, `is_draft`, `label_ids`, `module_ids`, `name`, `parent_id`, `priority`, `project_id`, `sequence_id`, `start_date`, `state_id`, `target_date`, `type_id`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed alongside the ids: `assignees` \(the assigned users\), `cycle` \(the cycle it belongs to\), `labels` \(the applied labels\), `modules` \(the modules it belongs to\), `parent` \(its parent work item\), `state` \(the work item's state object\), `type` \(its work item type\). Expansion is separate-key: `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it, so an id is never replaced by an object. An unknown value is a `400`. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent namespaces. Relation names are not valid `?fields=` tokens \(and vice versa\), and an expanded object survives field filtering — `?fields=id,name&expand=state` returns `id`, `name` and `state`. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |
| `deleted_at` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Deleted at. |
| `point` | number | No | v1 compatibility only. Point. |
| `sequence_id` | number | No | v1 compatibility only. Sequence id. |
| `sort_order` | number | No | v1 compatibility only. Sort order. |
| `archived_at` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Archived at. |
| `is_draft` | boolean | No | v1 compatibility only. Is draft. |
| `created_by` | string | No | v1 compatibility only. Created by. |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Items |
|   ↳ `id` | json | Id |
|   ↳ `name` | json | Name |
|   ↳ `identifier` | string | The human key, for example `PROJ-142`. It is the project's identifier joined to `sequence_id`, and it is what people paste into chat and commit messages. Use it with \[Get a work item by identifier\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-items/get-work-item-by-identifier\) when you don't have the project UUID. |

|   ↳ `label_ids` | array | Label ids applied to the work item. Empty array when unlabeled. |

| `display_name` | string | No | New human-readable label for the field. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form explanation of what the field is for, shown as helper text. |
| `property_type` | string | No | The kind of data the field holds: `TEXT`, `DATETIME`, `DECIMAL`, `BOOLEAN`, `OPTION`, `RELATION`, `URL`, `EMAIL`, `FILE`, or `FORMULA`. Changing the type of a property that already holds values changes what those values mean, so treat this as a migration rather than an edit — in most cases creating a new property and retiring the old one with `is_active: false` is the safer move. The full reference is on the \[properties overview\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-item-properties/overview#property-type-reference\). |
| `relation_type` | string | No | What a `RELATION` property points at: `ISSUE`, `USER`, `RELEASE`, or `RICH_TEXT`. Only meaningful when `property_type` is `RELATION`. |
| `options` | json | No | Write-only. Define `OPTION` choices inline, the same way you can on create. Each entry is a property option object with `name` required. For adding, editing, or removing a single choice on a live property, prefer the dedicated endpoints under \[Property options\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-item-property-options/list-property-options\) — they let you address one option by id instead of restating the set. The response always returns the resolved `options` array, never the payload you sent. |
| `is_multi` | boolean | No | Whether the field accepts more than one value. Turning it off on a property that already holds several values per work item is a narrowing change — check your data first. |
| `is_required` | boolean | No | Whether a value must be present. This applies going forward: existing work items with the field empty are not rejected retroactively, but the next edit will ask for a value. Pair it with a `default_value` so automated flows have something to fall back on. |
| `is_active` | boolean | No | Whether the property is offered. Setting `false` is the reversible way to retire a field — the definition, its options, and its recorded values all survive, and the field simply stops being offered. |
| `default_value` | json | No | The value applied when none is supplied. **Always an array**, even for a single-valued property — a `DECIMAL` field that defaults to `3` is sent as `\["3"\]`, not `3`. Send `\[\]` to clear the default. |
| `settings` | json | No | Free-form object holding type-specific configuration. The shape depends on `property_type`, so send the whole object rather than assuming keys — a partial `settings` object replaces the stored one. |
| `validation_rules` | json | No | Free-form object holding type-specific validation constraints. Same whole-object caveat as `settings`. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this field, for sync and import correlation. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `jira` or `linear`. Maximum 255 characters. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `default_value`, `description`, `display_name`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_multi`, `is_required`, `logo_props`, `name`, `options`, `property_type`, `relation_type`, `settings`, `validation_rules`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Item- Properties |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the property. This is the id you pass when attaching the property to a type or managing its options. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | The machine-readable slug for the property, derived by Plane. Read-only — it is not a create or update body field. Use it when you need a stable key in your own storage. |
|   ↳ `display_name` | string | The human-readable label shown wherever the property is rendered. This is the field you **write** on create and update. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | string | Free-form explanation of what the field is for. Surfaced as helper text next to the field. |
|   ↳ `property_type` | string | What kind of data the property holds. One of `TEXT`, `DATETIME`, `DECIMAL`, `BOOLEAN`, `OPTION`, `RELATION`, `URL`, `EMAIL`, `FILE`, or `FORMULA`. See the \[property type reference\]\(#property-type-reference\) below. |
|   ↳ `relation_type` | string | Relation type |
|   ↳ `is_multi` | boolean | Whether the property accepts more than one value. A multi-select severity list, a set of assignable reviewers, several linked work items. |
|   ↳ `is_required` | boolean | Whether a value must be present. Turning this on for an existing property affects work items edited from then on — it does not retroactively fill in the blanks. |
|   ↳ `is_active` | boolean | Whether the property is currently offered. Deactivating is the reversible alternative to deleting: the definition and its recorded values stay, the field stops being offered on new edits. |
|   ↳ `default_value` | array | The value applied when none is supplied. Always an array, even for a single-valued property — a decimal that defaults to `3` is `\["3"\]`, not `3`. |
|   ↳ `options` | array | For `OPTION` properties, the resolved list of choices. Each entry is a property option object with its own `id`, `name`, `is_default`, and `sort_order`. Manage them through \[Property options\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-item-property-options/list-property-options\), or define them inline when you \[create the property\]\(/api-reference/v2/work-item-properties/create-work-item-property\). |
|   ↳ `settings` | json | Settings |
|   ↳ `validation_rules` | json | Validation rules |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the property was created. |

### Plane Update a workspace work item property

Update a workspace work item property in Plane. Requires API v2.

#### Input

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --------- | ---- | -------- | ----------- |
| `apiKey` | string | Yes | Plane personal access token from Profile → API tokens. |
| `baseUrl` | string | No | Plane instance origin, optionally with a reverse-proxy path prefix. Defaults to https://api.plane.so. Do not include /api/v1 or /api/v2. |
| `apiVersion` | string | No | API version: v2 \(default\) for Plane Cloud and current commercial instances; v1 for Community Edition or older self-hosted instances. Unsupported operations or fields fail explicitly. |
| `bodyOverrides` | json | No | JSON overrides using the canonical input names for the selected API version. Preserves empty strings, null, and empty arrays; unsupported fields are rejected. |
| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `pk` | string | Yes | The property's id. |
| `display_name` | string | No | The label shown wherever the property is rendered. Maximum 255 characters. Renaming is safe for integrations that key on `id`. |
| `property_type` | string | No | One of `TEXT`, `DATETIME`, `DECIMAL`, `BOOLEAN`, `OPTION`, `RELATION`, `URL`, `EMAIL`, `FILE`, or `FORMULA`. Changing the type of a property that is already collecting values reinterprets what those values mean — prefer retiring the old property with `is_active: false` and creating a new one. |
| `relation_type` | string | No | For a `RELATION` property, what it points at. One of `ISSUE`, `USER`, `RELEASE`, or `RICH_TEXT`. Nullable. |
| `description` | string | No | Free-form explanation of what the property captures. Nullable — send `null` to clear it. |
| `is_required` | boolean | No | Whether a value must be supplied for this property. |
| `is_multi` | boolean | No | Whether the property accepts more than one value. |
| `is_active` | boolean | No | Set to `false` to retire the property without deleting it, and back to `true` to bring it into circulation again. |
| `default_value` | json | No | The value applied when none is supplied. Always an array. Send `\[\]` to clear it. |
| `options` | json | No | Write-only. For day-to-day option management — adding one choice, renaming another — use \[Property options\]\(/api-reference/v2/workspace-work-item-property-options/overview\), which addresses each option by id. |
| `settings` | json | No | Type-specific configuration. Its shape depends on `property_type`. |
| `validation_rules` | json | No | Type-specific validation configuration. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this property. Maximum 255 characters, nullable. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from. Maximum 255 characters, nullable. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `default_value`, `description`, `display_name`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_multi`, `is_required`, `logo_props`, `name`, `options`, `property_type`, `relation_type`, `settings`, `validation_rules`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Workspace- Work- Item- Properties |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the property. This is the id you use in a context's payload and when attaching the property to a workspace work item type. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Read-only companion to `display_name`. You never set it directly. |
|   ↳ `display_name` | string | The label shown wherever the property is rendered. This is the field you write. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | string | Description |
|   ↳ `property_type` | string | What kind of value the property holds. One of `TEXT`, `DATETIME`, `DECIMAL`, `BOOLEAN`, `OPTION`, `RELATION`, `URL`, `EMAIL`, `FILE`, or `FORMULA`. This is the one decision worth getting right up front — it determines what the other fields mean. |
|   ↳ `relation_type` | string | Relation type |
|   ↳ `is_required` | boolean | Whether a value must be supplied for this property. |
|   ↳ `is_multi` | boolean | Whether the property accepts more than one value. |
|   ↳ `is_active` | boolean | Whether the property is in use. Set it to `false` to retire a property without deleting it. |
|   ↳ `default_value` | array | The value applied when none is supplied. Always an array, even when `is_multi` is `false`. |
|   ↳ `options` | array | The choices for an `OPTION` property. Read-only on this object — manage the list through \[Property options\]\(/api-reference/v2/workspace-work-item-property-options/overview\), or seed it at create time with the write-only `options` body field. |
|     ↳ `id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `name` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `description` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Has Pages |
|     ↳ `sort_order` | number | Access |
|     ↳ `external_id` | string | Asset Id |
|     ↳ `external_source` | string | Asset Id |
|   ↳ `settings` | json | Settings |
|   ↳ `validation_rules` | json | Validation rules |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the property was created. |

| `is_active` | boolean | No | Send `false` to retire the type from pickers without deleting it — work items already classified with it keep their type. Send `true` to bring it back. |

Unrequested keys are **omitted** from the response, not returned as `null`, so absent means "not requested" and `null` means "actually null". `id` always comes back whether or not you name it. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400` that lists the valid set and suggests the closest match, so a typo can't silently cost you the saving. Requestable here: `created_at`, `description`, `id`, `is_active`, `is_default`, `is_epic`, `level`, `logo_props`, `name`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Workspace- Work- Item- Types |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the type. This is the id you send as `type_id` on a work item, and the id you pass when importing types into a project. |
|   ↳ `name` | string | Display name, for example `Bug`. Maximum 255 characters. |
|   ↳ `description` | string | What this type is for. Shown next to the type wherever it is picked in Plane, so it is worth writing for the people choosing, not for your integration. |
|   ↳ `is_active` | boolean | Whether the type can currently be selected. Deactivating a type retires it from pickers without deleting it or touching the work items already using it. |
|   ↳ `is_default` | boolean | Whether this is the workspace's default type. Read-only on create and update — change it with \[Mark a type as default\]\(/api-reference/v2/workspace-work-item-types/mark-default-workspace-work-item-type\). |
|   ↳ `is_epic` | boolean | Whether the type is an epic type. Read-only, and there is no body parameter for it: every type you create through this API is a standard work item type. |
|   ↳ `level` | json | Level |
|   ↳ `logo_props` | json | Logo props |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the type was created. |

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `workspace_slug` | string | Yes | Workspace slug from the Plane URL \(for example, my-team\). |
| `project_id` | string | Yes | The project the resource belongs to. Accepts the project UUID or its bare identifier, for example `ENG`. |
| `work_item_id` | string | Yes | The work item the resource hangs off. Accepts the work item UUID or its `PROJ-123` identifier. |
| `comment_html` | string | Yes | The comment html. |
| `access` | string | No | - `INTERNAL` - INTERNAL - `EXTERNAL` - EXTERNAL One of `INTERNAL`, `EXTERNAL`. |
| `external_id` | string | No | Your system's identifier for this record, for sync and import correlation. Maximum 255 characters. Nullable. |
| `external_source` | string | No | The system `external_id` came from, for example `github` or `jira`. Maximum 255 characters. Nullable. |
| `fields` | string | No | Comma-separated list of fields to return. Unrequested keys are **omitted**, not returned as `null`. `id` always comes back. Pass `all` for every requestable field. An unknown name is a `400`. See \[Sparse fields\]\(/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields\). Requestable here: `access`, `actor_id`, `comment_html`, `comment_stripped`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `edited_at`, `external_id`, `external_source`, `id`, `work_item_id`. |
| `expand` | string | No | Comma-separated relations to embed: `actor`. Expansion is separate-key — `?expand=state` keeps `state_id` and adds a `state` object next to it. `?fields=` and `?expand=` are independent: naming a relation in `?fields=` is a `400`, and expanded objects survive field filtering. See \[Expanding relations\]\(/api-reference/v2/expanding-relations\). |

#### Output

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ----------- |
| `result` | object | Plane V2 Work- Item- Comments |
|   ↳ `id` | string | Unique identifier for the comment. |
|   ↳ `work_item_id` | string | The work item this comment is attached to. Always matches the `work_item_id` in the request path. |
|   ↳ `comment_html` | string | The comment body, as HTML. This is the field you write. |
|   ↳ `comment_stripped` | string | The plain-text version of `comment_html`, derived server-side. It is what `?search=` matches, so markup never affects a search hit. Read-only — you never send it. |
|   ↳ `access` | string | Visibility of the comment. One of `INTERNAL` or `EXTERNAL`. `INTERNAL` keeps the comment inside the project team; `EXTERNAL` marks it as visible outside the team, for example on a published project. |
|   ↳ `actor_id` | string | Actor id |
|   ↳ `external_id` | string | External id |
|   ↳ `external_source` | string | External source |
|   ↳ `edited_at` | string | Edited at |
|   ↳ `created_at` | string | When the comment was created. |
|   ↳ `created_by_id` | string | Created by id |
|   ↳ `actor` | json | Actor |
